title: Positive solutions of the explicit formula for ζ(s): near-criticality and uniqueness
description:
Paper (51 pages) with its LaTeX sources and ancillary files (certificate scripts, parameter files and logs), a Lean 4 formalisation of the paper's logical spine with its axiom ledger, and a companion manuscript and three notes from the same project. Preprint, October 2026; not yet peer-reviewed.

We study the positive solutions of Weil's explicit formula with the archimedean data of the Riemann zeta function: pairs of positive measures, one on the zero side and one on the prime side beyond log 2/(2π). By linear-programming duality such pairs exist if and only if a positivity statement involving neither zeros nor primes holds; its slack κ* gives the optimal degree-one explicit-formula conductor bound qmin = exp(−2πκ*). We conjecture that ζ's own pair is the only solution; this does not imply the Riemann hypothesis, but makes it equivalent to existence. We prove it when the zero measure lives on the zeros of ζ and the origin, whatever the prime measure, when it lives on the zeros plus countably many summable points with the prime measure on the Bondarenko–Radchenko–Seip nodes, and when it is purely atomic with integer weights, whatever the prime measure. Certificates Ξ2PJ(t2), where the polynomial PJ is defined by Hermite interpolation at the first J prime powers, vanish at every zero of ζ; the one with J = 111 shows unconditionally that κ* ≤ 1.4291572·10−1060 and that every solution has ∫Ξ2 dμ ≤ 3.99·10−1060. Uniqueness would follow from asymptotic properties of these functions.

The Lean 4 formalisation (paper/anc/lean) states the headline results (Theorems A–D and the magic-function corollary) faithfully in Lean and proves them from Mathlib plus an explicit axiom ledger of 22 axioms (cited classical theorems, analytic steps proved in the paper but not yet formalised, and computer-assisted certificates); it contains no sorry, and its build and audit run in continuous integration.

Two theorems and their proofs, the zero-side support theorem (Theorem 3.6) and the extension of Theorem B from finitely to countably many extra zeros (Theorem 3.8), together with their consequences, were contributed by OpenAI's Astra during an independent review of an earlier version of the paper, and were then checked line by line by independent Claude referees. The certificates of the exact members added in version 1.2 (Proposition 5.7) were produced and independently refereed by Claude agents; their jet-subtraction approach was suggested by an analysis of the planar Cohn–Elkies certificate cited in the paper. The theorem on integer weights added in version 1.3 (Theorem 3.11) and its proof were produced and independently refereed by Claude agents. The rest of the mathematics, proofs and text was produced by AI agents (Anthropic's Claude Opus 5.5) under the author's direction; see the paper's AI-use statement.
